name: Aoheng
notes: Upper Mahakam River, above the Boh tributary, East Kalimantan (Smith 2017a: 127). Nearly identical to Seputan (p. 127); the two share the retention of medial *l before final *ʔ and *ŋ and are grouped together against Hovongan and Kereho (p. 138). Rows only from Tables 44-48 (pp. 137-138), the five changes Aoheng shares with Kereho and Seputan against Hovongan. The Aoheng forms of those tables have no final glottal stop where Kereho has one (oso, mose, ane, cela), as in Seputan; Smith does not state this for Aoheng and it is not a row. Glottolog: a dialect of Aoheng-Seputan (aohe1237).
inherit_note: Smith's Tables 37-38 have no Aoheng column: he uses 'Seputan data exclusively, rather than Seputan and Aoheng, since these two groups speak nearly identical languages' (p. 127). What Tables 44-48 do not show for Aoheng is assumed unchanged here, which is known to be too little: the Seputan rows of Tables 37-38 are not copied.

name: Punan Lisum
notes: East and North Kalimantan (Smith 2017a: 112). No Glottocode: Glottolog's Lisum (lisu1251) is filed as a dialect of Rejang Kayan, although its Punan subgroup Bukat-Ukit-Beketan-Lugat-Lisum (buka1263) is named after it (decision smith2017a-small-tables). A Punan dialect for Smith; rows only from Tables 32 and 34 (pp. 120, 122) and Figure 28.
inherit_note: Tables 29-30 have no column for this dialect; apart from the two statements about *ə (pp. 120-122) nothing is stated, and the rest is assumed unchanged from Proto-Punan.

name: Siang
notes: Data from Hudson (1967), as Smith cites it (2017a: 278). 'It appears that Siang belongs to the same group of Barito languages that Kadorih does' (p. 279). The only row is the reflex of *z, which Smith uses to argue that Kadorih *z > c is inherited and its j borrowed from Ngaju.
inherit_note: Smith states one reflex for Siang (*z); it has no column in Tables 56-57. Everything else is assumed unchanged from PMP, which the Siang forms of Table 82 show to be too little (they have ɾ for *l and o for *ə, as Kadorih does).
